temperature_range: 170–300 °C for TTIP/NH3 process, 250–450 °C for TDMAT/N2 process
summary: The study investigates the plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) of titanium oxynitride (TiOxNy) films using different precursors and process parameters. The O/N ratio in the films significantly affects their electrical properties such as conductivity, dielectric breakdown, and permittivity. The results show that the O/N ratio can be tuned by selecting appropriate process parameters and precursor/coreactant combinations. The study also compares the electrical and spectroscopic properties of films prepared with different precursors and process conditions.
evidence: The process parameters’ impact of the plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) method on the oxygen to nitrogen (O/N) ratio in titanium oxynitride (TiOxNy) films was studied. Titanium(IV)isopropoxide in combination with NH3 plasma and tetrakis(dimethylamino)titanium by applying N2 plasma processes were investigated. The O/N ratio in the TiOxNy films is found to be very sensitive for their electric properties such as conductivity, dielectric breakdown, and permittivity. Our results indicate that these PE-ALD film properties can be tuned, via the O/N ratio, by the selection of the process parameters and precursor/coreactant combination.
